widgets.name: Text
widgets.purpose: The one general text label for titles, names, metadata lines, counts, captions, stats, inline values, helper and footnote lines, toast and lightbox text. Named Text rather than Label so it does not collide with the shadcn/Radix form Label. Covers A's Text rows and B's Text rows. A's Description rows (helper text, footnote, settings row description, shortcut error line) are Text with as p, tone muted or danger, and live. Headings go to Heading and SectionHeader, search highlights to MatchHighlight, timestamps to RelativeTime, and the character counter to CharacterCounter. Sizes are in rem with 1rem = 14px. A's ten 0.5px steps are snapped to four named steps (B's fold, ties going up). Sources: A (labels.json rows and lens) and B (consolidated).
widgets.base: none (plain styled span, p or div; not a Radix primitive). Wrapped in a Radix Tooltip only when the tooltip prop is set.

props.name: as
props.description: Element. Default span. p for helper, footnote and error lines. div for block rows. Heading levels are not here; they belong to Heading.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Default false. True lets the user select and copy the text. Used for app version value (A SelectableText).

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Full value shown on hover and keyboard focus when the text is truncated, so the full name can be read.

props.name: live
props.description: Default off. Set polite on the shortcut error line so the rejection is announced when it appears (from A Description).

props.name: children
props.description: The text.

states: done (struck or faded, per the done axis)
matched (contains a MatchHighlight child inside a title or note)
unbound (tone inherit, italic, caller passes the text None)
announced (live polite or assertive on the shortcut error line)
widgets.role: none (span, p and div carry no role). Headings use Heading or SectionHeader.
widgets.keyboard: Not focusable. Where text is a tooltip trigger (truncated text, timestamp, reduced-motion status, truncated lightbox file name) the owning row or control must be tabbable (tabIndex 0) so keyboard users reach the tooltip. Escape dismisses it.
widgets.platform: Same widget on web and desktop. Differences are in content, not the widget. Desktop-only strings (Saved to, Data folder, capture rows, Low Power Mode, the macOS footnotes) do not appear on web. The sheet detail string '⌘Z puts it back' needs a per-platform string (Ctrl+Z on Windows and web). The native title tooltip is replaced by the Radix Tooltip on both. Web: browsers select text by default, so chrome labels need user-select none to match the desktop feel; the reference marks only app version value as selectable.
widgets.open: 1) Size steps: A's ten 0.5px steps are merged to xs, sm, md, base plus inherit (B's snap, ties up). Confirm the snap; it sets the rem values. 2) Conflict on the default size: A default 13 (md), B default base (14). Kept md (A). Confirm. 3) Conflict on the trash task title: A 13.5px regular (uncertain; measured estimate about 14px regular); B folds to base 14px regular. Kept base regular and flagged uncertain; it differs from the list title only in weight. Confirm. 4) Done task title is muted with strike (measured). Decide whether it takes the done-lamp colour (the brief) or stays muted. 5) Conflict on the done task note preview: A keeps faded (opacity 55%); B folds it to tone muted. Kept faded because it is a visible fade distinct from muted. Confirm. 6) Conflict on the unbound shortcut placeholder tone: A inherit (assumed), B muted. Kept inherit (colour not measured; it takes the keycap colour). Italic kept (catalogue lists Italic). Size inherits the keycap. Confirm. 7) Menu shortcut hint tone muted is assumed (not measured). 8) Attachment tile caption weight regular is assumed. 9) Lightbox status card helper: colour not measured; proposed onMediaMuted over the dark lightbox. It may be an error and need danger. Decide. 10) Lightbox position counter alpha 55% folded to 60%. Confirm. 11) Title-bar project pill owner: A puts it in Heading, B in Text with a display font. Merged to Heading (see Heading open). Confirm. 12) Shortcut error line live polite is proposed (A Description). 13) Settings row description 11.5px (A) folded to 12px (sm, B). Confirm.

widgets.name: Heading
widgets.purpose: Display-family (font-display) semibold title for window titles (settings, trash), the filter panel title, the sheet headline (dialog or sheet title and its accessible name), the selection summary headline in the multi-select inspector, and the title-bar project pill. Always tone primary. Sources: A (Heading rows, sizes 13.5, 14, 15, 16) and B (folded sizes: 13.5 to 14 ties up, 15 to 16 ties up). Conflict resolved: the title-bar project pill is in A's Heading (span) and B's Text (display font). It is placed in Heading here, because the display family is Heading's job.
widgets.base: none (styled h1, h2, h3, p or span; not a Radix primitive).

values.when: 14px (1rem). settings window title and trash window title (A 13.5 folded up), filter panel title, title-bar project pill (14px semibold).
16px (1.143rem). sheet headline (A 15 folded up, text-pretty), selection summary headline (16px semibold).
one line with ellipsis: window titles, panel title, project pill.
wraps onto more lines with text-pretty: sheet headline.

props.name: as
props.description: Default h2. h1 for the settings window title and the trash window title (B folds A's div to h1). h2 for the sheet headline on web and for the selection summary (A says p; see open). p gives no heading role. span for the title-bar project pill (a trigger, kept out of the heading outline).

props.name: children
props.description: Title content.

widgets.role: heading (level 1 to 3) when as is h1, h2 or h3. none for p and span.
widgets.keyboard: Not focusable. On desktop the settings and trash title bars are drag regions and take no keyboard focus. Dragging belongs to the title bar, not the text.
widgets.platform: Desktop: each sheet is its own window with no dimmed backdrop, so the sheet headline is that window title and renders as h1. The settings and trash titles sit in window title bars; the settings bar is a drag region. Trash drag behaviour is not recorded, so do not assume it drags. Web: no window title bars. The page or route title is the h1; a dialog title renders h2.
widgets.open: 1) Trash window title size: A says 13.5px (code text-[13.5px]; measured estimate about 14px, bold). B folds to 14px (sm). Font weight kept at semibold here. Confirm the size and weight. 2) Whether the trash title bar drags the window is not recorded. 3) Settings window title states (scrolled, recording) are window chrome; the catalogue does not say whether the text changes. 4) Conflict on the title-bar project pill owner: A Heading (span), B Text with font display. Merged to Heading. Span (no heading role) proposed because it is a trigger. Confirm. 5) Conflict on the selection summary element: A uses p (reference); B recommends h2 for landmark structure. Kept p pending confirmation. 6) Sheet headline size: A 15px, folded to 16px (md). Confirm.

widgets.name: SectionHeader
widgets.purpose: Eyebrow heading for a content block: an 11px semibold uppercase muted label with an optional hairline rule, an optional trailing slot (count text or add buttons), and an optional restore control with a changed dot. Covers the four section headers (plain, add toolbar, reset, discard) and the command group heading, which is the same eyebrow look in a listbox (inset listGroup). Sources: A (rule, restore, inset axes; label, trailing, active, onRestore props) and B (eyebrow size 11, caps, clear icon and label per restore kind, and the merge of the command group heading).
widgets.base: none; composes Text (size xs, weight semibold, tone muted, case uppercase) and an IconButton for the restore control.

values.when: no trailing rule. section header with add toolbar, section header with discard, command group heading.
hairline rule after the label. plain section header (shot-only, estimated) and section header with reset (trailing rule about x 917 to 1168, filter reset groups).
no restore control.

filter group heading (Sort, Show, Refine, Date). Restore icon restart_alt. Restores the group to its default (Sort to manual and asc, Show to all, Refine to any, Date to default). Labels like Clear sort, Clear show, Clear refine, Clear date.

settings group heading (Appearance, Tasks, Global, Main window, Capture bar, Screenshots, Application, Reset). Restore icon undo. Restores the values from when the window opened, not the shipped defaults. Label: Discard changes made since this window opened.
standard block heading (sidebar, inspector, filter and settings headings). Tracking 0.08em (caps).

group label inside a listbox (command palette): px inset and mt/mb spacing, no rule, rendered as div. Spacing kept as the reference shows it. Tracking folded to the single caps value 0.08em (A used 0.1em).

props.name: label
props.description: Heading text, for example Notes, Subtasks, Start with, Selected, Attachments, Sort, Show, Refine, Date, Appearance, Tasks, Global, Main window, Capture bar, Screenshots, Application, Reset. (B's title.)

props.name: trailing
props.description: Trailing slot: a count Text (Notes, Subtasks; numeric, muted; B's count prop) or add IconButtons (Attachments; B's actions prop). Add buttons suppress the rule.

props.name: active
props.description: True when the group is non-default or changed. Shows the changed dot and the restore control. Default false. (B's state idle|changed.)

props.name: onRestore
props.description: Runs the restore for reset or discard. Required when restore is not none. (B's onClear.)

props.name: restoreLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip for the restore control, for example Clear sort or Discard changes made since this window opened. On web, name the web baseline (for example last saved). (B's clearLabel.)

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level for block headings. Default h3. Use div for listGroup, where the listbox group labels itself.

states: changed (active true: dot and restore control shown)
widgets.role: heading (level from as) for block headings. none for listGroup, where the listbox group uses aria-labelledby pointing at the label.
widgets.keyboard: The header is not focusable. The restore control is a tab stop; Enter or Space runs it. After restore the control disappears, so focus moves to the group's first control or the header title, not lost to the page. Trailing add buttons are reached by Tab in order.
widgets.platform: Same widget. Desktop headers sit in the settings window; web in the settings page. The discard copy differs: desktop restores to the values when the window opened; web has no window open, so its restoreLabel names its own baseline (for example last saved). Filter groups are the same on both. Capture Screenshots header is desktop only.
widgets.open: 1) Changed dot colour: A reset header uses an accent dot; A discard header dot colour is not stated; B proposes primary ink (content-1). Accent is reserved for primary action and selection, so a changed-filter dot needs another token. Decision needed. 2) The plain header hairline is shot-only and estimated. Confirm before shipping. 3) The settings-general header passes look null; the catalogue does not say what null renders. Confirm it is this same header. 4) The discard header in shortcuts and about has no clear control in the recording; whether restore shows there is uncertain. 5) The Capture Screenshots header has no restore props (desktop only). 6) Tracking conflict: A 0.12em (block) and 0.1em (listGroup), B one caps value. Merged to 0.08em; confirm. 7) The clear control icon follows the restore kind (restart_alt for filter groups, undo for settings discard), per B.

widgets.name: Icon
widgets.purpose: One Material Symbols glyph widget for decorative chrome, status glyphs, chevrons, metadata glyphs, keycap glyphs, menu and command glyphs, and the tinted 32px glyph badge for sheets (tint axis; replaces A's IconBadge). Sizes are px with rem values; off-scale sizes snap to the nearest step with ties up (B): 13 to 14, 15 to 16, 19 to 20. Weight stays an axis (A: 200, 300, 400) because the measured 400 and 200 rows are visible; B's fixed 300 is not kept. Always pointer-events none, so a press reaches the parent control or drag region (B; replaces A's passThrough prop). Sources: A and B.
widgets.base: none (Material Symbols font, ligature names as in the catalogue; not a Radix primitive).

props.name: name
props.description: Material Symbols ligature name, for example drag_indicator, chevron_left, restart_alt. Required. For modifier keys the caller passes the platform glyph name.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional. Given, the icon has role img with this name. Omitted, it is decorative and aria-hidden. Required for the reduced-motion glyph. (Replaces A's decorative prop.)

states: expanded (rotate ccw90, driven by the caller)
error (caller swaps name to error; capture screenshot button)
widgets.role: img with a label when label is given (for example the reduced-motion status glyph). Otherwise none, aria-hidden.
widgets.keyboard: Never a tab stop. Inside a button, menu item or toggle, the parent holds focus and handles keys.
widgets.platform: Desktop only: window drag grip (desktop window chrome; web has no drag region), split-view markers (desktop split layout), capture clear, target and screenshot icons (capture bar; web has no screen capture), and settings capture pane icons. Keycap glyph: macOS desktop shows keyboard_command_key and keyboard_option_key; Windows and web show Ctrl and Alt as text, since the reference has no glyph name for either. Reduced-motion tooltip wording is per platform (see StatusIndicator). Sheets: desktop uses separate windows and web uses dialogs; the tinted badge is the same on both.
widgets.open: 1) Accent tone on the split-view marker (a state indicator; A) and the toast undo icon (follows the Undo button): accent is reserved for primary action and selection. B reads the split-view marker as a selection indicator and keeps accent. Decide the token and confirm. 2) Delete-confirm: the catalogue lists it under the accent sheet badge, but destructive actions use danger. Proposed: tint danger for delete-confirm. Confirm. 3) Weight conflict: A keeps 200, 300, 400 measured values; B folds everything to 300. Kept the axis. If the heavier stroke is not felt in review, collapse to 300 and drop the axis. 4) Colour not recorded for segment, settings tab, path folder, capture clear, capture target and capture screenshot: inherit assumed. Confirm in review. 5) Error glyph colour for the capture screenshot button is not recorded. 6) Reveal on focus-within for the attachment expand icon is an accessibility addition, not in the reference. 7) Split-view marker size 20 is assumed (no catalogue size). 8) Lightbox white at 70% folded to 60%. Confirm. 9) Sizes are in px in the reference; rem values are given here with 1rem = 14px.

widgets.name: StatusIndicator
widgets.purpose: Non-interactive 32px status cell holding a 20px glyph (A 19 folded up) that shows only while a status is active (reduced motion). Its explanation is a tooltip. Kept as its own widget (A) because it is a 32px cell with a conditional render and a tooltip, not an icon variant. B folds only the glyph into Icon xl.
widgets.base: Radix Tooltip (the reference used a title attribute).

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph name, motion_photos_off in the reference. Rendered by Icon at xl.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the status (required).

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Explanation shown on hover and on focus when the cell is focusable. Chooses between the Low Power wording and the Settings wording.

states: shown (only while the status is active)
widgets.keyboard: Not focusable in the reference. Recommend tabIndex 0 so the Radix Tooltip opens on focus and Esc closes it.
widgets.platform: Desktop only for the Low Power wording: 'Reduced motion active on Low Power Mode' is a macOS condition. Web cannot read Low Power Mode, so only the 'Reduced motion is on (Settings > General)' branch applies there, and that path names a desktop window, so web needs its own copy. Windows uses the OS reduced-motion setting.
widgets.open: 1) A hover-only tooltip is not reachable by keyboard or touch. Decide whether the cell is focusable (recommended tabIndex 0). 2) Whether web shows this indicator at all (it would come from prefers-reduced-motion) is a product decision. 3) The Settings > General wording needs a web version.

widgets.name: RelativeTime
widgets.purpose: Created or Updated time shown as a relative phrase, with the full date and time in a tooltip. Kept as its own widget (A) because it carries a dateTime value and an absolute tooltip; B folds it to Text with tooltip. Look: Text size sm, tone muted, weight regular.
widgets.base: Radix Tooltip, rendered in a time element.

props.name: at
props.description: Moment; becomes the dateTime attribute of the time element.

props.name: relative
props.description: Relative phrase shown in the row, for example 1w ago or 5d ago.

props.name: absolute
props.description: Full date and time shown in the tooltip, for example Nov 6, 2026, 9:00 AM.

widgets.role: time element (implicit role time). Tooltip role while open.
widgets.keyboard: Not focusable in the reference (hover only). Recommend tabIndex 0 so the tooltip opens on focus; Esc closes it.
widgets.platform: Same on both. The reference uses a native title tooltip (OS-drawn, own delay); the library uses Radix Tooltip on both, so behaviour matches across platforms.
widgets.open: 1) Native title versus Radix Tooltip changes the look and the delay. Deliberate change to confirm. 2) Relative phrase locale and absolute date format need a decision. 3) Created and Updated only; no due date (dropped by the brief).

widgets.name: CharacterCounter
widgets.purpose: Character count against the note limit. Switches to the danger tone when the count passes nearRatio of the limit (1800 of 2000 in the reference). Kept as its own widget (A) because the threshold switch is a felt behaviour; built from Text size xs, tabular numbers. B folds it to Text.

props.name: count
props.description: Current character count.

props.name: limit
props.description: Maximum length (2000 in the reference).

props.name: nearRatio
props.description: Share of the limit where the danger tone starts. Default 0.9.

states: near limit (danger tone, count above nearRatio of limit)
widgets.role: none. Optionally a polite status when the threshold is crossed.
widgets.platform: Same component. Desktop uses it in the capture bar note field (capture is desktop only); both platforms use it in the task inspector note editor.
widgets.open: 1) Confirm the threshold: the reference says chars > 90% of maxLength (strictly greater than nearRatio times limit). 2) Whether screen readers are told when the limit is approached: suggest a polite status only on crossing the threshold.

widgets.name: MatchHighlight
widgets.purpose: Inline highlight behind the text that matches the search query, in task titles and note previews. Kept as its own widget (A) because a highlight is a separate job from a text label (A's Text excludes search highlights) and its fill token is still open. B folded it into a Text emphasis axis; that axis is dropped here. Fill: accent-500 at 25% light and 30% dark, radius 3px, text inherits.

props.name: children
props.description: Matched text.

widgets.open: The fill is accent-500 at 25% light and 30% dark. Accent is reserved for primary action and selection, so the match highlight needs its own non-accent search highlight token (B). Decision needed. Placement and count of matches are approximate in the catalogue.

It belongs to the layout family (Stack or Inline). Its children are Text with tone muted, size sm (A 11.5 folded up to 12), numeric tabular. The wrapper must not set type styles itself. Same on web and desktop.
